# `ci_repair_adopt`

**Adopt a task as the CI repair.** Key a live task as the repair for a red branch and record the failing tests it owns, so the CI sentinel reuses it instead of filing another.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Capability | `ci_repair_adopt` |
| Side effect | `update` |
| Idempotency | natural |
| Retry safe | yes |
| Timeout | none |
| Preview | not supported |
| Defined in | [`src/commands/contracts/builtin.py`](../../../src/commands/contracts/builtin.py) |
| Contract fingerprint | `sha256:134f98dbb4312e27a58790e911a1968c17ec7e324c80a125133a42b09c0284ef` |

## Purpose

Make a task *the* repair that owns a red branch's failure.
[`ci_baseline_status`](ci_baseline_status.md) only reuses a repair it can
recognise, and a signature alone recognises a repair only while exactly the same
tests stay red. `ci_repair_adopt` gives a repair a durable record of the failing
tests it owns, so the sentinel keeps reusing it after a partial fix shrinks the
failing set, and files a new repair only for tests no live repair owns.

It is also how an operator hands the sentinel a repair filed by hand. Such a
task has no `ci-baseline:*` key, so the sentinel cannot see it and would file a
second deep-high repair beside it. Adopting it keys the task
`ci-baseline:<signature>:<n>` and records the whole failure CI shows right now:

    aq git ci-repair-adopt --project-id agent-queue --task-id <task-id>

The ownership rule is
[`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-16-ci-sentinel-repair-coverage-design.md`](../../superpowers/specs/2026-09-16-ci-sentinel-repair-coverage-design.md).

## When a playbook uses it

[`src/prompts/project_playbooks/agent-queue/ci-main-sentinel.md`](../../../src/prompts/project_playbooks/agent-queue/ci-main-sentinel.md),
rule `keep-main-green` step 3, runs it after [`ensure_task`](ensure_task.md) on
both `created` and `reused`, with `task_id: repair.task_id` and the failure
`baseline` said the repair owns (`ref`, `head_sha`, `repair_tests`,
`repair_checks`). Passing the observed failure means the step reads no CI of its
own. On a reused, already-recorded repair the step is a no-op (`unchanged`); on a
repair filed before repairs were recorded it writes the missing record.

## How it works internally

1. The executor builds `CiRepairAdoptArgs`; the adapter
   ([`src/commands/contracts/builtin.py:628`](../../../src/commands/contracts/builtin.py))
   re-enters `CommandHandler.execute`
   ([`src/commands/handler.py:872`](../../../src/commands/handler.py)), which
   dispatches `_cmd_ci_repair_adopt`.
2. `_cmd_ci_repair_adopt`
   ([`src/commands/ci_commands.py:471`](../../../src/commands/ci_commands.py)):
   - Requires `project_id` and `task_id`, and the task must belong to the
     project and be live — not `COMPLETED`, `FAILED` or `BLOCKED`, the statuses
     the sentinel counts as spent attempts.
   - Refuses a task whose `dedup_key` is not a `ci-baseline:<signature>:<n>`
     key: that key belongs to another ensuring pipeline.
   - A task that is already keyed *and* recorded returns `unchanged` with its
     record, before reading anything. The record is written once.
   - With neither `failing_tests` nor `failing_checks`, it reads `ref`'s CI
     through the same `_observe_ci_baseline` as `ci_baseline_status` and adopts
     the whole failure; anything but `red` is refused. Otherwise it uses the
     lists it was given, de-duplicated and sorted.
   - An unkeyed task is keyed `ci-baseline:<signature>:<n>`, `n` one past the
     highest index already used for that signature (`adopted`); a task already
     keyed keeps its key (`recorded`). The key is written before the record: a
     record on an unkeyed task would be invisible to the sentinel, while a keyed
     but unrecorded task still owns its exact signature.
   - `in_flight` names other live repairs that own part of the same failure —
     duplicates an operator may want to close. The command does not guess which
     one to keep.
3. `_outcome_of` (`builtin.py:547`) passes `adopted` / `recorded` / `unchanged`
   through and maps an `error`-carrying result to `rejected`.

## Side effects and persistence

Two writes on the task, both durable:

- `tasks.dedup_key`, only when the task had none, followed by a `task.updated`
  graph change event.
- The `task_metadata` row `ci_baseline_repair`:
  `{ref, head_sha, signature, failing_tests, failing_checks, recorded_at}`.

`ci_baseline_status` reads both back on every tick; nothing else is cached.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

| Outcome | Cause |
|---|---|
| `adopted` (success) | The task was unkeyed; it now carries a repair key and a record. |
| `recorded` (success) | The task already carried a repair key; the record was written. |
| `unchanged` (success) | The task was already keyed and recorded; nothing was read or written. |
| `rejected` | Missing `project_id` or `task_id`; unknown project; a task not in the project; a spent task; a task keyed for another pipeline; non-list `failing_tests` / `failing_checks`; or, when reading CI, a branch that is not red. |
| `unauthorized` | The capability gate refused `ci_repair_adopt`. |
| `contract_violation` | The dict did not satisfy `CiRepairAdoptValue`. |
| `input_resolution_failed` | A resolved input failed `CiRepairAdoptArgs`. |

`aq git ci-baseline-status --project-id <id>` shows which repairs the sentinel
considers `in_flight` after an adoption; `aq task show <task-id>` shows the key.

```json
  "type": "command",
  "rule": "keep-main-green",
  "title": "record_repair",
  "command": "ci_repair_adopt",
  "inputs": {
    "project_id": {"type": "literal", "value": "agent-queue"},
    "task_id": {"type": "binding_ref", "binding": "repair", "path": "task_id"},
    "ref": {"type": "binding_ref", "binding": "baseline", "path": "ref"},
    "head_sha": {"type": "binding_ref", "binding": "baseline", "path": "head_sha"},
    "failing_tests": {"type": "binding_ref", "binding": "baseline", "path": "repair_tests"},
    "failing_checks": {"type": "binding_ref", "binding": "baseline", "path": "repair_checks"}
  },
  "transitions": {
    "adopted": "keep-main-green--done",
    "recorded": "keep-main-green--done",
    "unchanged": "keep-main-green--done",
    "rejected": "keep-main-green--failed",
    "runtime_error": "keep-main-green--failed"
  }
}
```
